026 Round 1: ground, robots, props (Vela, 2026-10-20)

The old DecoKit city is the floor. This round ports its ground to the budget, re-colours it to the 26 Sep paintings, makes the robot set and its face data loadable, and checks the props. Evidence is Blender EEVEE renders (one warm sun, pale sky; not the game's lighting) with the same light on before and after, plus Latch's baseline and the old-city shots. Nothing here was driven in Unity: the ground and the faces are untested in the engine until Latch builds them.

1 · Ground: what is ported, and the budget

Total 27.24 MiB of the 30 MiB budget (new 21.92 MiB + the two terrazzo sheets reused from the kit, 5.32 MiB). Computed as texels x 1 byte (BC7 albedo and mask, BC5 normal) x 4/3 mips; each .meta sets BC7/BC5 on Standalone, aniso 16. Not measured on the Air (no Unity run). The old sheets would have been about 177 MiB as BC7 (4096 flags x 3 maps alone 64 MiB), so this is roughly a sixth of the old set, with no visible loss at play zoom (2.6 cm a pixel) and 2 mm a texel on the pavement at street level.

All new materials are URP Lit with m_Scale = 1 / tile, so a mesh whose UV is world metres tiles at real size. The textures are re-coloured with a per-channel power curve (granite: luminance curve plus the target hue) to the means below, so contrast and hue structure survive. The paintings' road is a violet-leaning grey (#797374, #696970) and their paving cream (#D3CAB5 to #E2D4C0); the old sheets were warmer-grey and bluer respectively. Brass stays a hairline: nothing here is brass.

Against what the world draws today

The 4 m repeat. Flags and the lawn repeat visibly from the air on large areas (the old city had it too). I softened the flag tone drift to 70 percent; the real fix is cheap and Latch's: give each ground patch a seeded UV offset and mirror, so the repeat never spans a block.

2 · Robots

RobotWaiter_Play, RobotNanny_Play and RobotShopkeeper_Play are new or newly built (the Waiter's FBX was catalogued but missing on disk; the Nanny and Shopkeeper had no Play copy), to the same standard as RobotButler_Play: same builder, L0 capped (Waiter 2,194, Nanny 2,590, Shopkeeper 2,339 triangles, against 14.6k to 19.7k), LOD1/LOD2 (about 25 and 10 percent), the head and its display kept as the movable parts DK_Robot*_Play_Head and _Head_Face, Signal_Red aliased to Beacon Rose, face materials DK_Face_Amber / DK_Face_Teal (already in the kit, shader DecoKit/RobotFace guid 0d01e3b1...). Porter and Butler Play copies were already right; I checked their parts, LODs and face materials and changed nothing.

Face data Latch can load

tools/decokit/art/robots/robot-faces.json (also in out/decokit/Data/ with RobotGlyphs.txt verbatim): 13 glyphs as rows, the five rigs (LED grid, corner, eye and mouth cells, neutral, moods, alarm face, idle range/turn/hold/home), the blink, mood and alarm timing, the face colours, and the atlas packing the shader reads. Source and provenance beside it; regenerate with python3 tools/decokit/robot_faces.py (--check for drift). The face driver (RobotFace.cs, RobotIdle.cs, 339 lines in the old project) is not ported: that is Latch's.

Needs Sky (section 15: no cartoon eyes). The old table has a heart, a star and a wink. They are kept in the data, marked needsSky and held out of each robot's default moods into moodsHeld, so nothing was dropped silently and turning one on is a one-line move. Plain LED shapes stay (round, wide, calm, arc eyes, smile, grin, beam, o). The alarm face (slanted lids, gritted teeth, red pulse) is kept: it is the robot's alarm cue and red is allowed on a small emissive display.

3 · Street props

The vending machines, Automat, planters, booths, sandwich board, post, ticket machine and signs are the old kit's own meshes, so the geometry is the floor already. What differs from the old city is material colour, shader and light, not the mesh. Checked: every material of all 276 pieces has a .mat (the only gaps are the three additive crossing-glow materials Latch draws by design); the retuned oxblood Enamel_Red and ochre Mustard (brief 007, for a colour gate that Sky dropped on 16 Oct) differ little from the old values at play zoom (A/B in the render set under round1/props/oldenamel-*), so I left them. Defects that are ours: none found in the meshes; Planter_Urn and Planter_Trough carry a bare shrub lump and orange blobs where the old Automat shot shows leafy topiary and flowering beds (a plants task, round 2); 0 vending machines, Automats or robots are placed in the world today.

4 · What Latch needs

  1. Ground meshes with UV = world metres (u = x, v = z). Materials by name from Kit/Materials: road and crossing deck DK_Ground_Asphalt; kerb top and face DK_Ground_Kerb (UV along the kerb, up the face, in metres); the 0.375 m gutter strip at the road edge DK_Ground_Gutter with u along the kerb and v 0 to 0.375 across; foot, pavement, quay, open and deck DK_Ground_Pavement (the civic square keeps DK_Pave_Civic); park, median, island DK_Ground_Lawn; park paths DK_Ground_Path; inlay bands DK_Terrazzo_Seafoam. No custom ground shader: URP Lit with a detail map is enough (asphalt uses _DETAIL_MULX2). The .mat files set m_Scale already.
  2. Break the repeat: a seeded UV offset (any value; the sheets are periodic) and mirror per ground patch.
  3. The materials only reach the project through a piece: Ground_Swatches (catalogued as a candidate, 16 triangles, carries all six roles) must be adopted by Splice so bun run kit copies the textures and .mats; it is also a prefab to eyeball the roles at true scale. Not placed in the world.
  4. Colour and the flat world roles: the textures carry the colour, so the looks file's flat asphalt #a5a2a8, pavement #f9efdc, kerb #ddd4c5 no longer apply on these meshes. The textured road is much darker (#79757A) than #a5a2a8; that is the paintings and the "too bright" call, but Glint should light with it, not against it.
  5. Robots: port RobotFace and RobotIdle (old project, Scripts/Robots); build the glyph atlas from RobotGlyphs.txt (8 x 8 tiles in a row, r lit, g height / 8, point filtered, clamp, global _DK_RobotGlyphs); drive the *_Face renderers by property block; rig numbers from robot-faces.json. DK_Face_Amber and DK_Face_Teal already use the shader. Use the _Play pieces; heads are *_Head.
  6. Import settings: the textures arrive with .metas (BC7 / BC5 on Standalone, aniso 16). The existing 4096 civic paving sheets are capped to 2048 by their Standalone override, so they are not a surprise cost.

5 · Open

  • Needs Sky: the heart, star and wink; and (information) the road's change from flat #a5a2a8 to a textured #79757A.
  • Not measured: frame time and BC7 sizes on the Air; both need Latch's build.
  • Did not touch: the legacy Pave_Flags, Kerb_Granite and TreePit pieces (they still point at the 4096 old sheets; adopting them would bring 64 MiB, so Splice should adopt DK_Ground_* instead or ask me to re-point them).
  • Changed in shared files: tools/decokit (ground_tex.py, ground_set.py, robot_faces.py, review026.py, mats.py, unity_mats.py, export_kit.py, play020.py, kit.py, run.ts); contracts/world/kit.json was refreshed by bun run kit --catalogue only.
